convoLines.text: "Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"This matters — Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"I count meals, not days. Three meals since the rain. Two since the alarm. Days are for people with calendars. I have a stomach. I need you to hear that."
"Still on what day it is."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Since Vivian died... I keep expecting to see Vivian at the fire. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sit apart to eat at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"I regret the ordinary days I rushed through. All those rural Vermont mornings I spent annoyed at small things. I'd pay anything for one annoyed morning now."
"Still on your regrets."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Vivian owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Vivian said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Nobody says Vivian's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"Its throat swells. That's Choir Toad telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"This one — Makhana (Fox Nut). Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Funny how that works."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Vivian was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About that question — Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"What's this about? Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still on whether you still sing."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? You'd know about that."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Vivian is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About that question — Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Just... be straight with me."
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Guest. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"About that question — What's something from your old life that's actually useful here? Hm."
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset. Do you understand?"
They nod. "Okay."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Between us — Still on your useful old-life skills."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? It'll pass."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — The Guest, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"All right. Show me when we work together."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"We need to — I'd like to learn something I can use today. Show me while you work, when you have a moment."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on teaching them something. That's the whole of it."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I wasn't an HVAC tech. I was a Veterinarian. You don't know what it's like, being the only nobody in a camp of somebodies."
"We went over this," Christian says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"What? No — I mean —" Christian stumbles. "It's... it's complicated. Can we not do this right now?"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"They took me. Hollow Belly — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."

deathBeat: d16: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Glasswing Darter is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d16: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Vivian Shin is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d16: 🕯️ Vivian Shin is dead — dehydration. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d16: The village's quarrel was with Vivian — and Vivian is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d16: 🕯️ The treeline is still torn up from the raid when the System's light comes for them. Nobody is ready. The light doesn't wait.
recoverHome: d17: That night, they bring Vivian home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d16: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d17: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 3,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.
d18: 📺 SYSTEM: "We have already cleared your morning. You are welcome. We require 300 kcal of tubers and your full attention. The fans love a cooking segment."
d18: 📺 SYSTEM: "We will keep practicing on our own." You decide, firmly, not to ask what that means.
d18: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d18: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
